overview: This 490-page file traces U.S. monitoring of Japanese radio from September 1941 to July 1943. Translated broadcasts and FBI, embassy, and FCC correspondence document Japan’s prewar diplomacy, early Pacific campaigns, wartime propaganda, and economic administration across occupied Asia. Later reports assess broadcast interference, intelligence value, and changing propaganda themes.
interest: The broadcasts capture Japan’s public messaging before Pearl Harbor, while monitoring reports reveal how U.S. officials used it for intelligence.
